rappels: About 5 rappels down the ridge, four single-rope and one double-rope, from existing fixed slings; a 70 m rope reaches most stations, and one party managed on a 50 m rope plus a tagline
descent_text: Descend by rappelling the ridge itself — most parties use a 70m rope to reach most stations comfortably; one reporting party got down on a 50m rope with a tagline. Existing fixed rap slings have been reported along the route.
approach: Via the multi-day Goodell Creek approach to a camp on the Chopping Block ridge (~6,400 ft) or the col separating the peak from the main Picket Range; from there, walk and scramble (some exposed 3rd class) southwest to the base of the ridge.
overview: The peak's classic technical route: 4 pitches of alpine rock up the northeast ridge, established by the Firey party in 1970, with a steep 5.5 crux about 100 ft below the summit.
beta: The route climbs the ridge in 3-5 pitches (typically done in 4) at 5.5. Rock quality ranges from highly questionable to pretty solid. The line involves a rightward traverse around overhanging walls, narrow exposed grass ledges, and ridge-crest climbing on somewhat loose alpine rock before a steep crux section roughly 100 ft below the summit.
gear: single rack of cams to #2 Camalot
